summary.text: A 57-year-old female with chronic pulmonary aspergillosis diagnosed in May 2020 presented to A&E eight times within one year with small volume haemoptysis, cough productive of green sputum, dyspnoea and lethargy. Past history included allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonization, asthma, bronchiectasis, osteoporosis with vertebral compression fractures and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. She was a never smoker with no occupational exposures, and her listed medications included prednisolone 5 mg once-daily and several inhalers.

CT showed minor bronchiectatic changes in 2012, a first left upper lobe cavity in 2014, bilateral cavities and nodules by 2015, and in October 2024 persistent bilateral upper lobe cavitating lesions, new nodularity and multiple aspergillomas. Serum Aspergillus IgG was raised and sputum PCR was positive three times. BAL antigen was positive in 2018, 2019 and 2021, sputum culture grew AF, and the TR34/L98H resistance mutation was detected.

Voriconazole was stopped after one week for visual hallucinations, itraconazole was discontinued in December 2019 for progression on CT, and posaconazole was stopped in September 2020 after resistance detection. A 3-week IV LAB course in 2020 improved her clinically and LAB was later given as required until January 2024. The MDT advised an IV echinocandin course; she declined inpatient caspofungin, and weekly rezafungin via OPAT was agreed.

She received a 400 mg IV loading dose and eleven 200 mg IV weekly doses between January and April 2025. Nausea, anorexia and myalgia occurred, blood-tinged sputum occurred without frank haemoptysis, and blood tests and creatine kinase stayed stable or normal. Symptoms improved, with no A&E attendances afterwards, IgG fell from 165 to 98 mgA/L, and CT showed small improvement in the cavities.
